text:
marta: Heads-up — we're getting a tight hotspot in us-east1: lots of 0.125 GPU pods landing on rack-3, other racks underutilized, then attach failures and rapid evictions. Started ~03:45 UTC.
li: Confirmed. Telemetry shows rack affinity density for tiny pods spiked to 0.88 and evictions in training namespace up 4x. Suspect recent packing heuristics change that prefers NVLink locality.
deep: Pulled a sample scheduler trace: 
```
I0501 03:45:12 scheduler.go:402] Evaluate pod small-train-21 on node gpu-3a: locality_bonus=0.7, pack_penalty=0.1, final_score=0.8
I0501 03:45:12 attach-controller.go:70] Attach attempt failed for small-train-21: attach timeout to gpu-3a (allocatable=0.0)
I0501 03:45:13 scheduler.go:450] Reschedule small-train-21 -> scoring other nodes
```
deep: The scheduler keeps favoring locality_bonus and ignores fragmentation cost; pack_penalty seems too small for tiny slots. Also saw the new NVLink affinity label `gpu.redwood/nvlink-cohort=alpha` applied cluster-wide yesterday.
marta: NVLink affinity was meant for big-gang jobs; shouldn't pull tiny independent pods. Could the weighting config not respect pod_size_threshold?
li: Yep — config toggled for gang >1 previously, but a default override set in bootstrap introduced a global weight. That explains tiny pods getting preference.
deep: Quick mitigation: reduce `scheduler.weights.locality` to 0.1 for training namespace in us-east1 via configmap rollout; also mark warmpool nodes on racks B/C with `gpu.redwood/accept-tiny=true` so scheduler has eligible targets.
marta: Ops, can you apply node label script? `kubectl label nodes -l rack in (B,C) gpu.redwood/accept-tiny=true --overwrite`
ops-bot: runbook invoked: ops/label-warmpool-tiny #22 -> us-east1. Applying labels across 8 nodes.
infra-bot: deploy job started: scheduler/weight-adjust #1202 -> canary (us-east1)
li: While the short-term label + weight tweak helps, we should change the heuristic to penalize rack-level fragmentation. Suggest `fragmentation_score = sum(used_slots^2)` style penalty so concentrated tiny pods incur cost.
deep: Agreed. I'll draft change: 1) add fragmentation penalty, 2) enforce `pod_size_threshold` gating for NVLink affinity, 3) add unit tests and a regression perf test that simulates tiny-pod churn.
marta: Also run a backfill rebalancer overnight to move some tiny pods across racks to reduce hot tails. Prefer a controlled rearranger instead of mass deletes.
ops-bot: warmpool scale command issued: `ops scale warmpool --region us-east1 --count 6 --size tiny` -> done.
li: Cost note: we saw double-scheduling spikes where attach failed and pods retried on other nodes — added ~1.2 GPU-hours in last 2 hours. Track for chargeback.
deep: Canary for scheduler tweak in canary cluster passed basic checks. Rolling to prod in 12m. Will also add telemetry: `scheduler.fragmentation_penalty` and alert if >0.4.
marta: Postmortem tasks: 1) revert global NVLink default override (li), 2) implement fragmentation penalty (deep), 3) ops playbook to label warmpools for tiny slots (ops), 4) rebalancer controller RFC (marta).
li: PR: https://git.redwood/scheduler/pull/1202 — includes config gating and weight bump.
infra-bot: deploy job succeeded: scheduler/weight-adjust #1202 -> prod (us-east1)
ops-bot: labels applied and warmpool scaled. Early telemetry shows rack spread ratio improving and pending count falling.
marta: Thanks team. I'll keep monitoring and will open the postmortem doc after we stabilize. :thumbsup:
